breaker.definition: For odd prime q with q∤6, I0(q)={-3x^2/2:x∈F_q}, I1(q)={-3x^2/2-1/2:x∈F_q}; Break(q) iff I0(q)∪I1(q)=F_q.
breaker.equivalence: This is the scalar branch-covering predicate of the reconstructed parity quadratic readout; the existing split-hyperbola/K4 theorem is support mathematics for the same predicate.
breaker.result: q_b=5 is the unique nonsingular odd breaker characteristic for B=3.
breaker.proof_summary: One-orbit support gives q<=5; q odd and q∤6 leaves q=5, and I0(5)={0,1,4}, I1(5)={1,2,3} cover F_5.

capacity.definition: For the translated scalar readout Z_H(r)=H+(3r^2+epsilon(r))/2, k_*(q) is the sharp maximum consecutive q-coprime run in the breaker phase.
capacity.proof_summary: Existing quadratic-ramification theorem gives one zero in a 2q period at an extremal critical class, hence sharp 2q-1; substitute q_b=5.
capacity.guard: This is breaker-coprime/divisibility capacity, not the separate actual native prime-incidence island cap.

transverse_saturation.definition: Sat(q) iff the union of the root sets of the unordered packet modulo q equals F_q^*; q must be an odd nonsingular prime q∤6.
transverse_saturation.proof_summary: Three quadratics contribute at most six roots, so q-1<=6 and q<=7. The nonsingular odd candidates are 5,7; exact root partitions are q=5: {1}|{2,3}|{4}, q=7: {2,3}|{1,6}|{4,5}.

longitudinal_boundary.definition: For odd k>=5 on grade window W_k={0,...,k-1}, take distinct u,v,w with u≡v (mod2), w≢u (mod2). Maximize |w-u||w-v| and read the unordered distance pair at a maximizer.
longitudinal_boundary.theorem: max |w-u||w-v|=(k-2)(k-4), and every maximizing distance multiset is {k-4,k-2}.
longitudinal_boundary.result: At k_*=9 the invariant longitudinal boundary pair is {5,7}.
longitudinal_boundary.proof_summary: For w outside [u,v], parity forces the two nearest same-parity endpoints at one side and the furthest opposite-parity index at the other, giving distances k-4,k-2; interior w or any inward shift strictly decreases one factor. Reflection gives the only symmetric alternatives.
